pairs.why: B's locomotive has a proper grille cowcatcher, connecting rods linking the drivers, and a coupled coal tender, while A's front is a solid slab block with oddly sized wheels.
B's wagon has a hitching tongue attached to the front axle and an open bonnet with hoops over a box resting on its wheels, while A's cover has a strange hole and no clear tongue linkage.
A's rocket has a real exhaust nozzle that the flame comes out of and fins mounted on the body, while B's flame comes from a flat black base under a loose-looking nose ring.

A's folding camp chair copies the real card's X-frame, with the seat sling hung between tube rails and the back uprights continuing from the legs, while B's armrest and X-leg joints are vaguer about how they would fold.
In A, the life ring's reflection sits far out in the water away from the ring, but B's ring and rope coil hang on posts and the rope runs between them.
B's calculator keys are all blank, so it couldn't be used, while A has labeled digit and operator keys like the real card.
A's lasso loop is joined to the coil by a real knot, but B's loop just ends at a white ferrule on the rope with no honda knot to slide through.
B's cat sits on all four paws with its tail growing from the rump, while A's tail seems to come out of the side of its body.
